summary: Wenjiang Ding worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Peking University and under Qichao Liang (~1918–1929), later holding a post at Peking University from around 1931 to 1934.

Specializing in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Wenjie Duan studied at Sichuan Fine Arts Institute and the Central Academy of Fine Arts. He served at the Dunhuang Academy as archaeological group head (1946), fine arts head (1950), and director (1991).

Wenjie Qin works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Qin completed a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Wei-ming Tu and studied under Diana L. Eck, Masatoshi Nagatomi, Charles Hallisey, and Robert M. Gimello.

Werner Abraham was a linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Vienna. He held posts at Illinois (~1965–1967), Tübingen (1970–1971), and Groningen (1971), alongside guest professorships at Cologne, Vienna (2001), and Lund.

Werner Sundermann worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1967–1970), the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (~1970–1992), and the Free University of Berlin (~1993–2000).
Wes Borton works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Borton studied at East Carolina University under Derek F. Maher and also studied at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

Whalen Lai specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned a BA at International Christian University and a PhD at Harvard, later teaching at the University of Illinois (~1975–1976) and UC Davis (~1976–2008).

Whitney Cox specializes in Indology and religious studies. Cox studied at the University of Virginia and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock, Wendy Doniger, and others, later serving as professor at Chicago (~2013).

Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Ceylon and earned a PhD from SOAS. He held posts at the University of Ceylon (1952–1973) and the University of Kelaniya (~1956–1986).

Wilburn Hansen is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. Hansen pursued a master's program at the University of Colorado Boulder and studied at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

Wilfred Cantwell Smith was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD from Princeton. He taught at Forman Christian College (1940–1946) and held chairs and directorships at McGill University (1948–1951) and Harvard University (1964–1985).

Wilfrid Sellars was a philosopher who studied at Michigan, Buffalo, and Oxford. He taught at the University of Iowa (1938–1946), the University of Minnesota (1947–1958), Yale University (1958–1963), and held a professorship at Pittsburgh (1963–1989).

Wilhelm Deecke worked in linguistics and Indology, earning a doctorate from Leipzig and studying in Berlin under Albrecht Weber, Franz Bopp, and others. He directed several schools, including Ernestinenschule (1855–1870), Gymnasium Bouxwiller (1884), and Lycée Albert-Schweitzer (1889).

Wilhelm Dilthey was a philosopher who studied at Heidelberg University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held academic posts at the University of Basel (~1866–1868), Kiel (~1868–1871), Breslau (~1871–1882), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1882–1905).

Wilhelm Geiger was a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies who earned his PhD under Friedrich von Spiegel at Erlangen-Nuremberg. He served as professor at Erlangen-Nuremberg (from 1891) and the University of Munich (1920–1924).

Wilhelm Gesenius specialized in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at the University of Helmstedt (~1803–1806) and the University of Göttingen (~1806), subsequently holding posts at Göttingen (~1806–1809) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1810–1842).

Wilhelm Grube was a scholar of sinology and linguistics who studied at Saint Petersburg and earned a PhD at Leipzig under Georg von der Gabelentz. He held posts at the Asiatic Museum, Ethnological Museum of Berlin, and Berlin University (1884–1908).
Wilhelm Gundert was a scholar in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Karl Florenz and held an academic post at the University of Hamburg from around 1927 to 1945.

Wilhelm Halbfass was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed his doctorate at the University of Göttingen. He served as an assistant at Göttingen (~1968–1970) and was a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1982–2000).

Wilhelm Havers was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held academic appointments at the universities of Leipzig (~1913–1915), Bern (~1915–1920), Würzburg (~1920–1929), Breslau (~1929–1937), and Vienna (~1937–1953).
